title: "Design API"
description: "Configured benchmark and research design families."
jupyter: python3
---

```{python}
import inspect

from pypanelsim import designs

def show(names):
    for name in names:
        value = getattr(designs, name)
        print(f"{name}{inspect.signature(value)}")
```

## Canonical benchmarks

```{python}
show((
    "CanonicalPanelConfig",
    "classic_factor_design",
    "weak_factor_design",
    "synthetic_control_design",
    "factor_synthetic_design",
    "time_series_design",
    "mixed_factor_design",
    "make_canonical",
    "available_canonical_designs",
))
```

Direct-draw functions have the same base name without `_design`:
`classic_factor`, `weak_factor`, `synthetic_control`, `factor_synthetic`,
`time_series`, and `mixed_factor`.

`CanonicalPanelConfig` controls control and treated unit counts, pre and post
periods, the linear-effect slope, and noise variance. Family-specific arguments
control loading overlap, active donor share, or autoregressive persistence.

## Baker design

```{python}
show(("BakerPanelConfig", "baker_design", "baker"))
```

The configuration gives calendar years, adoption years, cohort sizes, dynamic
effect slopes, and noise scales. `n_units` may exceed the sum of cohort sizes;
remaining units are never treated.

## F-test designs

```{python}
show((
    "FTestTemporalConfig",
    "FTestCohortConfig",
    "ftest_temporal_profile",
    "ftest_cohort_profiles",
    "ftest_temporal_design",
    "ftest_cohort_design",
    "ftest_temporal",
    "ftest_cohort",
    "available_ftest_temporal_designs",
    "available_ftest_cohort_designs",
))
```

The temporal configuration controls one cohort and one effect path. The cohort
configuration controls three adoption periods, their unit shares, correlated
error scales, and periodic time effects.

## Adaptive pooling designs

```{python}
show((
    "LepskiiPanelConfig",
    "lepskii_profiles",
    "lepskii_design",
    "lepskii",
    "available_lepskii_designs",
))
```

The configuration controls nine default adoption cohorts, cohort shares,
fixed-effect scales, two-way error correlation, and periodic time terms. The
named variant controls only the cohort-event effect surface.

## Conditional and latent trend designs

```{python}
show((
    "ATTDMConditionalConfig",
    "ATTDMLatentConfig",
    "ATTDMClusteredConfig",
    "att_dml_design",
    "att_dml",
    "available_att_dml_designs",
))
```

The design name determines which configuration type is valid:

| Names | Configuration |
|---|---|
| `conditional_parallel_trends`, `conditional_parallel_trends_nonlinear` | `ATTDMConditionalConfig` |
| `latent_parallel`, `latent_nonparallel` | `ATTDMLatentConfig` |
| `clustered_arma` | `ATTDMClusteredConfig` |

Passing a configuration from the wrong row raises a type error.

## Regression-compression designs

```{python}
show((
    "RegressionCompressionConfig",
    "regression_compression_design",
    "regression_compression",
    "AnscombePanelConfig",
    "anscombe_design",
    "anscombe",
    "available_anscombe_designs",
))
```

`RegressionCompressionConfig` controls sample size, adoption, effect profile,
heterogeneity, fixed-effect and trend scales, and AR(1) error. The Anscombe
family places heterogeneity at zero, unit, time, or cohort-time level.

## Composite benchmark

```{python}
show((
    "GSynthCompositeConfig",
    "gsynth_composite_design",
    "gsynth_composite",
))
```

The four component weights correspond to factor, time-series, sparse-synthetic,
and two-way fixed-effects outcome components. This family is a package stress
test, not a paper reproduction.

## Seed inputs

All direct-draw functions accept `seed` or `rng`. Research-family direct draws
also accept named `streams` where shown in their signature. The simulator
constructor always permits `SimulationSeeds` through `simulate(streams=...)`.
